text: NASA launched a one and a half billion dollar space telescope. The first pictures came back blurry.
Hubble's main mirror had been ground to the wrong shape. Its edge was too flat by two point two microns. About one fiftieth of the thickness of paper.
The instrument used to test it was assembled wrong, by one point three millimetres. So the mirror was made perfectly, to the wrong measurement.
In nineteen ninety-three, astronauts flew up and installed corrective optics. Basically, glasses.
Dave volunteered to hold the eye chart.
